prompt: Describe a plan that you had to change recently

and how you felt about the change

part2.question: Describe a plan that you had to change recently

segments.v: I want to talk about a plan I changed last month. My friends and I planned to go camping in Ba Vì for two days. We prepared for many weeks. We booked a campsite and borrowed tents. But three days before the trip, there was news about a big storm. There would be heavy rain in the mountains. Our parents didn't allow us to go. So we changed our plan. We had a camping night at Linh's house. We put a tent in her living room, cooked hotpot and watched films. The next day we walked around West Lake. At first I was very sad. But the new plan was very fun. I felt safe because the storm was very strong. We will go to Ba Vì later.

part3.question: Why do people sometimes change their plans?

segments.v: Because something unexpected happens, like bad weather or illness. Sometimes they have a better plan.

bad weather, illness, a traffic jam, or a sudden problem at work. Sometimes it's new information; if you find out a place is closed or much more expensive than expected, you adjust. People also change plans when a better
comes up, or when other people's needs take
like a family member needing help. And sometimes,
it's just a change of mood; the plan made on Monday doesn't feel right by Saturday.

part3.question: Do young people change plans more often than older people?

segments.v: Yes, I think so. Young people are more free and they change their mind easily.

segments.v: Yes, it can. Sometimes the new plan is better than the old plan.
